stem: If two charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ are separated with distance '$d$' and placed in a medium of dielectric constant $K$. What will be the equivalent distance between charges in air for the same electrostatic force?
solution:
$F = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{q_1q_2}{kd^2}$ (in medium), $F_{air} = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\dfrac{q_1q_2}{d'^2}$

$F = F_{air} \Rightarrow kd^2 = d'^2 \Rightarrow d' = d\sqrt{k}$

stem: A particle executes simple harmonic motion between $x = -A$ and $x = +A$. If time taken by particle to go from $x = 0$ to $\dfrac{A}{2}$ is $2$ s; then time taken by particle in going from $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$ to $A$ is:
solution:
Using the reference circle: from $0$ to $A/2$, $\omega t_1 = \pi/6$; from $A/2$ to $A$, $\omega t_2 = \pi/3$.

$\dfrac{t_1}{t_2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow t_2 = 2t_1 = 2\times 2 = 4$ s

A gas can be taken from A to B via two different processes ACB and ADB.

When path ACB is used $60$ J of heat flows into the system and $30$ J of work is done by the system. If path ADB is used work done by the system is $10$ J. The heat flow into the system in path ADB is:
solution:
$\Delta Q_{ACB} = \Delta W_{ACB} + \Delta U_{ACB} \Rightarrow 60 = 30 + \Delta U \Rightarrow \Delta U = 30$ J

$\Delta U_{ADB} = \Delta U_{ACB} = 30$ J (state function)

$\Delta Q_{ADB} = \Delta U_{ADB} + \Delta W_{ADB} = 30 + 10 = 40$ J

stem: A long straight wire of radius $a$ carries a steady current $I$. The current is uniformly distributed across its cross section. The ratio of the magnetic field at $\dfrac{a}{2}$ and $2a$ from the axis of the wire is:
solution:
Inside ($r = a/2$): $B_1\cdot 2\pi\dfrac{a}{2} = \mu_0\dfrac{I}{4} \Rightarrow B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi a}$

Outside ($r = 2a$): $B_2\cdot 2\pi(2a) = \mu_0 I \Rightarrow B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi a}$

So $B_1 = B_2 \Rightarrow 1:1$
